title: Talking about past experiences / Kasa mu nsɛm a ɛda akyi
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛka nsɛm a ɛda akyi, yɛnkyɛnkyɛ yɛbɛka 'ɔda' anaa 'meda' sɛ ɛda no wɔ hɔ ma yɛn ara anaa yɛn ho ahyɛdeɛ. Wɔ English mu, sɛ ɛbɛka nsɛm a ɛda akyi, wɔde 'present perfect' ('have visited') ka, na ɛnyɛ Twi mu. Nokware no, wɔ English mu wɔde 'have + past participle' ma nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ berɛ biara, nanso wɔ Twi mu yɛnkyɛnkyɛ yɛde 'ɔda' anaa 'meda' ma nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ berɛ bi ho. Faako a, wɔ English mu, ɛnyɛ nea ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'present perfect' ma nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ berɛ bi ho, sɛ 'yesterday' anaa 'last year'.
rule: Sɛ wɔbɛka nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ English mu, yɛde 'present perfect' na yɛbɛka: have/has + past participle. Yɛde no ma: 1) nsɛm a ɛda akyi a ɛnyɛ berɛ bi ho (I have visited Paris), 2) nsɛm a ɛda akyi na ɛwɔ hɔ ma yɛn ara anaa yɛn ho ahyɛdeɛ (She has lost her keys), 3) na wɔde mmoa 'ever', 'never', 'already', 'yet', 'just', 'before'. Sɛ ɛbɛyɛ nea ɛnyɛ, yɛde 'have not' (haven't) anaa 'has not' (hasn't). Sɛ ɛbɛyɛ nsɛm a ɛso, yɛde 'Have you ever...?' na yɛbɛka 'Yes, I have' anaa 'No, I never have'. Ɛnyɛ nea ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'present perfect' ma nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ berɛ bi ho (yesterday, last week, in 2010). Wɔ nhwɛso no mu, yɛde 'past simple' (visited, went). Sɛ ɛbɛyɛ A2, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔhu 'past participle' no ho nhia wɔ mmoa a wɔkyerɛ no pii mu (go-gone, eat-eaten, see-seen, have-had).

concept_examples.text: I have visited Mexico.
She has never eaten sushi.
Have you ever seen that movie?
concept_examples.translation: Wohwɛ film bi a wɔde akyerɛ wɔ?

concept_examples.text: We have already finished our homework.

common_error.explanation: Ɛbɔ nea ɛbɔ no ara na wɔ Twi mu, ɛnyɛ nea ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'present perfect' ma nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ berɛ bi ho, sɛ 'yesterday'. Sɛ ɛbɛyɛ nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ berɛ bi ho, yɛde 'past simple' (visited). Sɛ ɛnyɛ berɛ bi ho, yɛde 'present perfect' (have visited). Faako a, 'present perfect' na berɛ bi ho = ɛnyɛ.

levels.label: Present Perfect with 'ever' and 'never'
levels.translation: Present Perfect na 'ever' na 'never'

examples.original: Have you ever been to London?
examples.note: Yɛde 'ever' ma nsɛm a ɛso ma nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ berɛ biara mu.

examples.original: I have never tried Thai food.
examples.note: 'Never' de wɔ 'have' na 'past participle' ntɛm, na ɛka 'ɔbaabi' wɔ ɔmanfo nyinaa mu.

examples.original: She has never flown in a plane.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi hæz ˈnɛvər floʊn ɪn ə pleɪn/
examples.note: Faako a, 'flown' ne 'fly' no 'past participle', na ɛne mmoa biara.

levels.label: Present Perfect with 'already' and 'yet'
levels.translation: Present Perfect na 'already' na 'yet'

examples.note: 'Already' de wɔ nsɛm a ɛyɛ mu, na ɛka 'already' (sɛ ɛda pɛ).

examples.original: Have you bought the tickets yet?
examples.note: 'Yet' de wɔ nsɛm a ɛso na nsɛm a ɛnyɛ mu, na ɛwɔ kyerɛɛ no mu, na ɛka 'aane'.

examples.original: We haven't finished our project yet.
examples.note: Wɔ nsɛm a ɛnyɛ mu, 'yet' de wɔ kyerɛɛ no mu, na ɛka sɛ ɛnda yɛn ho ahyɛdeɛ.

levels.label: Past Simple vs. Present Perfect
levels.translation: Past Simple vs. Present Perfect

examples.note: 'Present perfect' de wɔ nsɛm a ɛda akyi a ɛnyɛ berɛ bi ho.

examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə pəˈruː ɪn tuː ˈθaʊzənd nɪnˈtiːn/
examples.note: 'Past simple' de wɔ nsɛm a ɛda akyi wɔ berɛ bi ho, sɛ 'in 2019'.

examples.original: She has lived in Madrid for two years.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi hæz lɪvd ɪn məˈdrɪd fɔːr tuː jɪrz/
examples.translation: ɔda wɔ Madrid mu ma awia awia.
examples.note: 'Present perfect' de wɔ 'for' + berɛ mu ma nsɛm a ɛda akyi na ɛwɔ hɔ.

examples.translation: ɔhwɛɛ ɔno adwuma nyɛmɛ nea ɛda akyi.
examples.note: Wɔ 'past simple' mu, 'see' yɛ 'saw', na ɛde wɔ berɛ bi ho.

translations.tw: Kasa mu nsɛm a ɛda akyi

title: Making Plans and Arrangements / Kɔntɔkɔntɔ ne nnwoma
bridge: Wɔ Spain bere a, yɛnka present tense anaa future tense (ir a + infinitivo) kyerɛw kɔkɔ ne nnwoma. Wɔ Twi a, yɛnka 'present continuous' (I'm meeting) kyerɛw kɔkɔ ne nnwoma a wɔare nea ɛdi asɛm, na 'be going to' (I'm going to visit) kyerɛw adwene. Fa akwantu: wɔ Twi a, yɛnntɔn present simple tense kyerɛw futures a ɛyɛ pa a, nanso wɔ Spain a, yɛnka no kyerɛw kɔkɔ ne nnwoma (ɛ. 'Te llamo mañana' → 'I'll call you tomorrow', ɛnyɛ 'I call you'). Anaa, 'will' yɛnka no kyerɛw adwene a yɛbɛyɛ no nkyɛn.
rule:
Saa wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛka kɔkɔ ne nnwoma wɔ Twi a, yɛnka nsɛm nnɛ ha:

1. **Present continuous** (am/is/are + -ing): kyerɛw kɔkɔ ne nnwoma a wɔare nea ɛdi asɛm, ne bere ne lugar. Ɛ. 'I'm seeing the doctor at 3.' (Mɛkɔ no nkyɛn).

2. **Be going to** (am/is/are going to + infinitivo): kyerɛw adwene anaa kɔkɔ a ɛnyɛ nea ɛdi asɛm. Ɛ. 'We're going to visit our grandparents.' (Yɛbɛkɔ no nkyɛn).

3. **Will** (will + verbo base): kyerɛw adwene a yɛbɛyɛ no nkyɛn wɔ bere a yɛrekɛ kyerɛw no. Ɛ. 'I'll help you with that.' (Adwene a yɛbɛyɛ no nkyɛn).

4. **Would like to** (would like to + infinitivo): kyerɛw adwene a ɛyɛ pa anaa ɛyɛ kwan. Ɛ. 'Would you like to come to my party?'

Tumi hu sɛ wɔ Twi a, yɛnntɔn present simple tense kyerɛw futures a ɛyɛ pa a (ɛnne Spain a). Yɛnka 'be going to' anaa 'present continuous' kyerɛw kɔkɔ.

concept_examples.text: I'm meeting my friend at the cinema tonight.

concept_examples.translation: Wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛkɔ me mmemua a ɛbɛba no?
concept_examples.phonetic: wʊd juː laɪk tə kʌm tə maɪ ˈbɜːrθdeɪ ˈpɑːrti

common_error.wrong: I meet my friend at the cinema tonight.
common_error.correct: I'm meeting my friend at the cinema tonight.
common_error.correct_alt: I'm going to meet my friend at the cinema tonight.
common_error.explanation: Asɛm bi wɔ hɔ wɔ Spain a, yɛka 'Quedo con mi amigo' wɔ present simple tense kyerɛw kɔkɔ a ɛbɛba no. Wɔ Twi a, present simple tense nni kyerɛw futures a ɛyɛ pa a; kyerɛw kɔkɔ a ɛdi asɛm no, yɛnka present continuous (I'm meeting) anaa 'be going to' (I'm going to meet).

levels.label: Expressing Future Plans with 'going to'
levels.translation: Kyerɛw kɔkɔ a ɛbɛba no ne 'going to'

examples.original: I'm going to visit my grandma this weekend.
examples.phonetic: aɪm ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ˈvɪzɪt maɪ ˈɡrændmɑː ðɪs wiːkˈend
examples.translation: Mɛkɔ me mama ho wɔ weekend a ɛbɛba no.
examples.note: Yɛnka 'be going to' + infinitivo kyerɛw adwene anaa kɔkɔ a ɛnyɛ nea ɛdi asɛm. Wɔ Spain a, yɛnka 'ir a + infinitivo'.

examples.original: She's going to start a new job in June.
examples.phonetic: ʃiːz ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə stɑːrt ə njuː dʒɒb ɪn dʒuːn
examples.translation: Onyame a ɛbɛba no, ɔbɛkɔ hwɛ no ho wɔ June.
examples.note: Hwɛ sɛ 'going to' nni hɔ wɔ person a, na 'be' (is, am, are) na ɛyɛ.

levels.label: Making Fixed Arrangements with Present Continuous
levels.translation: Kyerɛw nnwoma a ɛdi asɛm ne present continuous

examples.original: I'm seeing the dentist at 4:30 tomorrow.

examples.translation: Mɛkɔ dentist ho anɔpa a ɛbɛba no wɔ 4:30.
examples.note: Present continuous kyerɛkyerɛ sɛ nnwoma no adi asɛm. Wɔ Spain a, yɛnka 'voy' anaa 'tengo cita'.

examples.original: We're having dinner with the Smiths on Friday.
examples.phonetic: wɪər ˈhævɪŋ ˈdɪnər wɪð ðə smɪθs ɒn ˈfraɪdeɪ

examples.note: Saa nnwoma a ɛdi asɛm ne bere ne lugar a, present continuous yɛ nsɛm a ɛyɛ pa wɔ Twi.

levels.label: Inviting and Responding to Suggestions
levels.translation: Adwene ne kwan

examples.original: Would you like to join us for lunch?
examples.phonetic: wʊd juː laɪk tə dʒɔɪn ʌs fɔːr lʌntʃ
examples.translation: Wopɛ sɛ wɔbɛkɔ yɛn ho kwan wɔ lunch?
examples.note: Yɛnka 'would like to' kyerɛw adwene a ɛyɛ pa. Wɔ Spain a: '¿Te gustaría...?'

examples.original: Sure, I'd love to. What time?
examples.phonetic: ʃʊr aɪd lʌv tə wɒt taɪm
examples.note: Kwan a ɛyɛ pa. 'I'd love to' yɛ 'I would love to' a ɛyɛ kwan.

examples.original: Sorry, I can't. I have another appointment.
examples.phonetic: ˈsɒri aɪ kænt aɪ hæv əˈnʌðər əˈpɔɪntmənt

title: Giving advice and recommendations / Kyerɛkyerɛ ne nnyinasosɛm a wo de ma obi
bridge: Wɔ Twiriso, sɛ yɛbɛka kyerɛkyerɛ a, yɛnkyea subjunctive (te recomiendo que vayas, deberías ir). Wɔ English, subjunctive ntɛm wɔ ‘recommend’ anaa ‘suggest’ nkyɛn; yɛnkyea verb so abase anaa object + infinitive: ‘I recommend you go’, ‘I suggest you try’. Yɛnkyea ‘should’ (deberías) a ɛso aka pɛpɛɛpɛ wɔ ‘must’ kɛse. Kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ den paa ne sɛ wɔbɛka subjunctive a wɔde sia Twiriso: ‘I recommend that you go’ yɛ nokware, nso ‘I recommend you to go’ yɛ kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ den sɛeɛ, efisɛ wɔ English ‘recommend’ nni hɔ a wɔde ‘to’ di infinitive a ɛwɔ object so.
rule:
Sɛ wubɛka kyerɛkyerɛ ne nnyinasosɛm wɔ English A2 a, hwɛ mfonua no:
1. **Should / Shouldn't + verb abase**: ma kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛte saa. Mfonua: 'You should eat more vegetables.' 'You shouldn't stay up late.' (kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ den). Wɔnntɛm (he should, no he shoulds).
2. **You could + verb abase**: ma nnyinasosɛm a ɛte saa anaa nnyinasosɛm. Mfonua: 'You could try yoga.'
3. **I recommend / I suggest + that + subject + verb abase** (ntɛm ‘to’ ne subjunctive a ɛwɔ ending). Mfonua: 'I recommend that you see a doctor.' Wɔhwehwɛ gerund: 'I recommend seeing a doctor.' anaa 'I suggest trying this.'
4. **How about + gerund (-ing)?**: ma nnyinasosɛm a ɛyɛ den. Mfonua: 'How about going for a walk?'
5. **Why don't you + verb abase?**: ma nnyinasosɛm a ɛwɔ hwɛso. Mfonua: 'Why don't you take a break?'
Hwɛ: ntɛm ‘must’ ma kyerɛkyerɛ, ɛso aka kɛse; ‘must’ ne nnyinasosɛm. Ma nnyinasosɛm a ɛte saa, hwɛ ‘could’ anaa ‘might’. Hwɛ sɛ wɔ ‘recommend’ ne ‘suggest’ nkyɛn, ntɛm ‘to’ a ɛwɔ object so: 'I recommend you to go' yɛ kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ den.

concept_examples.text: You should drink more water.
concept_examples.translation: Wokɔ so a wɔmfa nsu pii.

concept_examples.text: I recommend that you talk to the teacher.
concept_examples.translation: Mekyerɛ wo a woka kyerɛ no kyerɛwɔ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˌrekəˈmend ðæt juː tɔːk tə ðə ˈtiːtʃər/

concept_examples.text: Why don't you try it?
How about studying with us?

common_error.wrong: I recommend you to go to the doctor.
common_error.correct: I recommend that you go to the doctor.
common_error.correct_alt: I recommend going to the doctor.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twiriso, yɛka ‘te recomiendo que vayas’ anaa ‘te recomiendo ir’, nso wɔ English, wɔ ‘recommend’ nkyɛn, ntɛm infinitive a ɛwɔ ‘to’ a ɛwɔ object so. Kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ nokware ne ‘recommend + that + subject + verb abase’ anaa ‘recommend + gerund’. Kyerɛkyerɛ yi kɔ so efisɛ akorɛ bɛka ‘te recomiendo a ti ir’ (a ɛte sɛ ‘recommend you to go’). Sɛ wubɛtwa kyerɛkyerɛ yi a, hwɛ: ‘recommend’ di ‘that’ anaa ‘-ing’, ɛmmom ‘to’.

levels.label: Basic advice with should
levels.translation: Kyerɛkyerɛ a ɛte saa ne should

examples.translation: Wokɔ so a wɔmfa awerɛho pii.
examples.note: Hwɛ ‘should’ + verb abase. Wɔ Twiriso, ‘deberías’ + infinitive.

examples.note: Kyɛfa a ɛyɛ den ne ‘shouldn't’ + verb abase. Wɔnntɛm ma ɔha.

examples.original: We should study for the test.
examples.translation: Yɛkɔ so a yɛbɛsom ma no nnwom.
examples.note: ‘Should’ nntɛm: I should, you should, we should.

levels.label: Suggestions with could and how about
levels.translation: Nnyinasosɛm ne could ne how about

examples.original: You could try the new restaurant.
examples.translation: Wokɔ so a wɔprɛko ɔdwuma foforo.
examples.note: ‘Could’ ma nnyinasosɛm a ɛte saa, ɛso aka pɛpɛɛpɛ wɔ ‘should’.

examples.original: How about going to the park?
examples.translation: Dɛn na yɛbɛtoa so yɛbɛkɔ akyɛdeɛ?
examples.note: Wɔ ‘How about’ nkyɛn, hwɛ gerund (-ing).
Wohwɛ ‘could’ wɔ hwɛso ma nnyinasosɛm a ɛyɛ den.

levels.label: Formal recommendations with recommend and suggest
levels.translation: Nnyinasosɛm a ɛyɛ den ne recommend ne suggest

examples.original: I suggest that you take a break.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ səˈdʒest ðæt juː teɪk ə breɪk/
examples.note: Hwɛ ‘that + subject + verb abase’ (ntɛm ‘to’ ne subjunctive a ɛwɔ ending).

examples.original: They recommend staying at the hotel.
examples.note: Hwɛ gerund sɛ wɔnni subject a ɛte saa.

examples.original: The teacher suggested that we practice every day.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈtiːtʃər səˈdʒestɪd ðæt wiː ˈpræktɪs ˈɛvri deɪ/
examples.translation: No kyerɛkyerɛwɔ kaa sɛ yɛbɛtoa so yɛbɛsom da.
examples.note: Wɔ ɔkɔm hyia a, hwɛ ‘that’ + verb abase (ntɛm ‘practiced’). Yi ne mmerɛ.

translations.tw: Kyerɛkyerɛ ne nnyinasosɛm a wo de ma obi

title: Expressing opinions / Kyerɛwoɔ asɛm (Mepɛ, Mesuro)
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛnka 'mesuro sɛ' ne 'me pɛ sɛ' sɛ wɔyɛ adwuma mma, nanso wɔ English mu, ɛnyɛ mma: 'I think' yɛ nkɔsoɔ pii ne yɛ ma fa kyerɛwoɔ ne adwene, na 'I believe' kyerɛkyerɛ adwene kyɛ kyɛw ne anidaso. Ɛyɛ ɛhwɛ kɛse sɛ wɔatwa 'Me pɛ sɛ' sɛ 'I think that', nanso wɔ English mu, 'that' yɛ deɛ ɛsɛ sɛ woatwa ne sɛ wɔnka pii. Enti, wɔ English mu, ɛkyerɛw kronkron ne sɛ: subject + verb + object, na ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔtɔn 'in' anaa 'of'. Fa akɔntɔ a ɛwɔ asɛm no mu ne sɛ wɔnntɔn 'that' sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wɔtɔn no ho adwuma.
rule:
Saa yɛbɛka yɛn adwene wɔ English mu A2 kɛseɛ mu no, yɛbɛka nsɛm a ɛte saa:
- 'I think (that) + sentence' – sɛ yɛbɛka yɛn adwene ne yɛn adwene.
- 'I believe (that) + sentence' – sɛ yɛbɛka yɛn adwene anaa yɛn adwene.
- 'In my opinion, + sentence' – ɛso wɔ kyerɛwoɔ mu, nanso ɛyɛ den wɔ akasa mu.
Abrofo a wɔyɛ den sɛn: 'I guess' (mesuro) ne 'I suppose' (mesuro), na wɔte saa ara na wɔyɛ den.
Saa: 'that' yɛ deɛ ɛsɛ sɛ woatwa ne sɛ wɔnka pii. Ɛkyerɛw kronkron ne sɛ: subject + verb + object. Mmom sɛ wɔbɛka 'of' anaa 'on' akyi 'think/believe'. Wɔnka 'I think in that', nanso wɔka 'I think that' anaa 'I think'. Adwuma: 'I think (that) it's a good idea', 'I believe (that) he is right'. Wɔ kyerɛwoɔ a ɛnyɛ den mu, ɛbɛyɛ sɛ wɔde 'do you think?' tɔ so: 'It's a good idea, do you think?'

concept_examples.text: I think it's going to rain.
I believe you are right.
In my opinion, this movie is great.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔ me nkitahodi mu, phim no yɛ paa.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ əˈpɪnjən ðɪs ˈmuːvi ɪz ɡreɪt/

concept_examples.text: I guess we can try again.
concept_examples.translation: Mesuro sɛ yɛbɛtumi ayɛ no bio.

common_error.wrong: I think in that it is good.
common_error.correct: I think that it is good.
common_error.explanation: Ɛyɛ ɛhwɛ kɛse sɛ wɔatwa Twi 'me pɛ sɛ' sɛ 'I think in that', na wɔtɔn 'in' akyi. Wɔ English mu, 'think' ne 'believe' mmom sɛ wɔtɔn object akyi. Mmom sɛ wɔtɔn 'in' anaa 'on'. Enti, sɛ woka 'I think it is good' no ara nea ɛyɛ den paa wɔ kyerɛwoɔ mu.

levels.label: Basic opinions with I think
levels.translation: Kyerɛwoɔ asɛm kɛseɛ ne I think

examples.translation: Mesuro sɛ English no yɛ mma.
examples.note: Fa 'I think' + sentence na mmom sɛ wɔtɔn 'that' wɔ kyerɛwoɔ mu.
Saa: mmom sɛ wɔtɔn 'that' sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wɔtɔn no.
Verb 'be' tɔ so sɛ subject no: I am, you are, we are.

levels.label: Stronger opinions with I believe
levels.translation: Kyerɛwoɔ asɛm a ɛsoɔ ne I believe

examples.translation: Mesuro sɛ ɛyɛ paa sɛ wɔdii.
examples.note: Wɔ hɛn mu 'believe in' kyerɛ sɛ wɔwɔ adwene mu, nanso sɛ wɔbɛka adwene no, wɔfa 'believe that'.

examples.original: I believe that he is honest.
examples.note: Wɔ hɛn mu 'that' yɛ deɛ ɛsɛ sɛ woatwa ne sɛ wɔnka pii.

examples.original: I believe this is the best option.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ bɪˈliːv ðɪs ɪz ðə bɛst ˈɒpʃən/
examples.translation: Mesuro sɛ ɛyɛ deɛ ɛsoɔ paa.
examples.note: Fa 'this' sɛ ɛwɔ hɔ; 'that' sɛ ɛwɔ far.

levels.label: Giving opinions and asking others
levels.translation: Kyerɛwoɔ asɛm ne kyerɛwoɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ

examples.original: In my opinion, the food is delicious.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ əˈpɪnjən ðə fuːd ɪz dɪˈlɪʃəs/
examples.translation: Wɔ me nkitahodi mu, ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa.
examples.note: Kyerɛwoɔ no yɛ den paa ne wɔfa no wɔ asɛm no anim, na wɔtɔn comma.

examples.original: What do you think about this plan?
examples.phonetic: /wɒt duː juː θɪŋk əˈbaʊt ðɪs plæn/
examples.translation: Deɛ wopɛ soɔ no kyerɛ me?
examples.note: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wɔkyerɛ wo adwene, fa 'What do you think about...?'
'I guess' yɛ den ne kyerɛ sɛ wɔwɔ adwene mu anaa wɔsuro.

title: Agreeing and Disagreeing / Kɔbɔ ne Ankɔbɔ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛ ka sɛ yɛkɔbɔ, yɛka 'Mekɔbɔ' na sɛ yɛbɛ ka sɛ yɛankɔbɔ, yɛka 'Menkɔbɔ'. Nanso wɔ English, wɔka 'I agree' ne 'I disagree'. Wɔka 'so do I' ne 'neither do I' so sɛ wɔbɛka sɛ wɔkɔbɔ ne sɛ wɔankɔbɔ, na sɛ wɔka 'I am agree' no ara na ɛyɛ den. Hwehwɛ sɛ 'agree' yɛ verb, na ɛnyɛ adjective, enti woka 'I agree' na ɛnyɛ 'I am agree'.
rule: Sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ wɔ English, wuka 'I agree' anaa 'I think so'. Sɛ wubɛka sɛ wuankɔbɔ, wuka 'I disagree' anaa 'I don't think so'. Sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ ne kɔbɔ a wɔaka, wuka 'So do I' anaa 'Me too'. Sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ ne ankɔbɔ a wɔaka, wuka 'Neither do I' anaa 'Me neither'. Wɔka 'Exactly' anaa 'That's right' so sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ pii. Wɔka 'I'm not sure' so sɛ wubɛka sɛ wuankɔbɔ paa. Hwehwɛ sɛ 'agree' yɛ regular verb: I agree, you agree, he/she agrees. Sɛ wubɛka kyerɛɛ wɔkɔbɔ, wuka 'Do you agree?'

concept_examples.text: I agree with you.
I disagree with that idea.
So do I.
Neither do I.

common_error.explanation: Errɔ no fi asɛm so adi mfehemem sɛ wɔ Twi, 'kɔbɔ' ka 'kɔbɔ' + adjective, na mmara no kyerɛ sɛ wɔbɛka 'I am agree'. Nanso wɔ English, 'agree' yɛ verb, enti ɛntɔn so wɔhyɛ 'to be' verb no. Sɛ wubɛto so, hwehwɛ sɛ 'agree' yɛ verb, na ɛnyɛ adjective. Dii kan sɛ 'I agree' anaa 'I don't agree'.

levels.label: Basic Agreement and Disagreement
levels.translation: Kɔbɔ ne Ankɔbɔ a ɛyɛ den

examples.note: Kasa bi a ɛyɛ den sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ. Wɔka no wɔ nnipa pii ne nnipa akɔto mu.
Kasa bi a ɛyɛ den sɛ wubɛka sɛ wuankɔbɔ. Di kan sɛ wɔmmu wɔ a wɔbɛka no.
Kasa bi sɛ wubɛka sɛ biribi yɛ nokware.
Kasa bi a ɛyɛ den sɛ wubɛka sɛ wuankɔbɔ.

levels.label: Agreeing with Positive and Negative Statements
levels.translation: Kɔbɔ ne kɔbɔ ne ankɔbɔ a wɔaka

examples.note: Wɔka no sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ ne kɔbɔ a wɔaka. Kyekye: I like coffee. So do I.
Kasa bi a ɛyɛ den ne a ɛso pɛpɛɛpɛ sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ ne kɔbɔ a wɔaka.
Wɔka no sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ ne ankɔbɔ a wɔaka. Kyekye: I don't like tea. Neither do I.
Kasa bi a ɛyɛ den ne a ɛso pɛpɛɛpɛ sɛ wubɛka sɛ wukɔbɔ ne ankɔbɔ a wɔaka.

levels.label: Polite Disagreement and Expressing Doubt
levels.translation: Ankɔbɔ a ɛyɛ pɛ ne adwene a ɛyɛ den

examples.note: Kasa bi a ɛyɛ pɛ sɛ wubɛka sɛ wuankɔbɔ.
Wɔka no sɛ wubɛka sɛ wuankɔbɔ paa.
Kyerɛɛ wɔkɔbɔ no sɛ wuhwɛ adwene no mu na wuankɔbɔ.
Kasa bi a ɛyɛ pɛ sɛ wubɛka sɛ wuankɔbɔ.

title: Describing Daily Routines / Kasa tumi ahyε wɔ da biara
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka 'me nte me rekɔ' anaa 'me rekɔ' wɔ reflexive verbs ho. Wɔ English, wɔnntusa reflexive wɔ routine ho: simple 'I get up'. Na wɔ Twi, yɛde subject no bɛhyɛ no ankasa ('me rekɔ'), nanso wɔ English no, ɛsɛ sɛ woka 'I' ('I have breakfast'). Difference bi nso ka: wɔ English, wɔ actions a ɛbɛyɛ den den, wɔde present simple with -s wɔ third person ho ('he gets up'), na frequency adverbs ('always', 'usually') de wɔ verb no anim, nnnka wɔn ahyɛ wɔ kyerɛw no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ wɔ Twi ('siempre me levanto' vs. 'I always get up').
rule: Saa wɔka ahyε wɔ da biara wɔ English no, wɔde present simple. Structure no ne: Subject + verb (with -s for he/she/it) + complement. Frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) de wɔ main verb no anim, nanso wɔde wɔn ahyɛ verb 'to be' no ho. Time expressions sɛ 'in the morning', 'at night' de wɔ sentence no nsi anaa nkyɛn. Suhyɛ sɛ wɔ English no, ɛnyɛ nea ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɔ subject no.

concept_examples.text: I wake up at six every morning.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ weɪk ʌp æt sɪks ˈɛvri ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: She usually takes a shower in the evening.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃi ˈjuʒuəli teɪks ə ˈʃaʊər ɪn ðə ˈivnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: We have breakfast together at home.
They always go to bed at eleven.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔn nyinaa gyaa wɔn ho wɔ 11:00 daa da.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ ˈɔlweɪz goʊ tu bɛd æt ɪˈlɛvən/

common_error.explanation: Errors a ɛyɛ den wɔho ne sɛ wɔde -s no kɔm wɔ third person singular ho. Wɔ Twi no, conjugation no susuw (se despierta), nanso wɔ English no, wode -s anaa -es ka. Error bi nso ne sɛ wɔde subject no kɔm ('Wakes up'), nanso wɔ English no, ɛsɛ sɛ wode no. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wobɛyɛ no a, suhyɛ sɛ: wɔ he/she/it ho, de -s ahyɛ verb no.

levels.label: Morning Routine
levels.translation: Morning Routine

examples.note: De 'get up' ma wɔto so wɔ bed no ho, nnnka 'wake up' a ɛne sɛ wato so wɔ sleep no ho.
Wɔ English no, wɔde possessive adjective 'his' ka, nnnka reflexive 'se'.
'Have' de wɔ food ne drinks ho, nnnka 'drink'.

levels.label: Work and Study Activities
levels.translation: Work and Study Activities

examples.original: They go to work by car.
examples.note: De 'by' + means of transport without article (by car, by bus).
Adverb 'after' de wɔ kyerɛw no nkyɛn, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ wɔ Twi.
Wɔ he/she/it ho, verb 'watch' susuw ho sɛ 'watches'.

levels.label: Adverbs of Frequency
levels.translation: Frequency Adverbs

examples.original: I always eat lunch at noon.
examples.note: Adverb 'always' de verb 'eat' no anim, nnnka wɔn ahyɛ wɔ kyerɛw no nkyɛn.

examples.original: He usually reads the news in the morning.
examples.phonetic: /hi ˈjuʒuəli ridz ðə nuz ɪn ðə ˈmɔrnɪŋ/
examples.translation: Ono kenkan news wɔ morning daa.
examples.note: Adverb 'usually' de subject ne verb no ntɛm.

examples.translation: Wɔn nyinaa ntɛw wɔn ho afeɛ a midnight atɔ so.
examples.note: 'Never' yɛ negative, entumi de 'don't' wɔ same sentence no ho.

translations.tw: Kasa tumi ahyε wɔ da biara

title: Talking about health and symptoms / Kasa kɛ adwene ho
bridge: Wɔ Twi akyerɛ, yɛnka ‘tener’ de ma ka ho asɛm: ‘tengo dolor de cabeza’, ‘tengo fiebre’. Wɔ English akyerɛ, anka di kan: yɛnka ‘have’ (‘I have a headache’) de ma ka ho asɛm na yɛnka ‘feel’ de ma nnomuonyam (‘I feel sick’). Anka a wɔ ho berɛ a wɔka ‘I have cold’ nti, na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔka ‘I have a cold’, efisɛ wɔ English akyerɛ, ka ho asɛm a wɔde ‘cold’ anaa ‘headache’ ka no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ den na ɛyɛ nokware.
rule:
Ma ka ho asɛm na adwene ho asɛm A2 kyrɛ wɔ English no, hwɛ anidaso no:

1. **Have + ka ho asɛm:** Yɛnka ‘have’ (na ɛnyɛ ‘tener’ a ɛyɛ nokware) ma ka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ ɛho: ‘I have a cold’ (me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den), ‘I have a headache’ (me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den), ‘I have a toothache’ (me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den). Fa ‘a’ ma ɛho no biara.

2. **Feel + adwene:** Ma adwene ho asɛm no, yɛnka ‘feel’ + adwene: ‘I feel tired’ (me nnomuonyam), ‘I feel sick’ (me nnomuonyam), ‘I feel dizzy’ (me nnomuonyam).

3. **Adwene a ɛyɛ den:** Sɛ adwene no ɛnyɛ den a, ɛbɛyɛ sɛ woka ‘I have pain in my back’ (me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den) anaa ‘my back hurts’ (me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den).

4. **Verbo 'hurt':** Yɛnka ‘hurt’ ma ka ho asɛm: ‘My head hurts’ (me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den), ‘My stomach hurts’ (me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den).

5. **Kyerɛw wo ho asɛm:** Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wokyerɛw wo ho asɛm a, yɛnka ‘What's wrong?’ (Աnka wo ho asɛm?), ‘Are you okay?’ (Wohwɛ?), ‘How do you feel?’ (Wode ntease?).

6. **Adwuma:** Ma adwuma no, yɛnka ‘should’ anaa ‘shouldn’t’: ‘You should see a doctor’ (Ɛsɛ sɛ wofa akwantufoɔ), ‘You shouldn’t eat that’ (Ɛnyɛ sɛ wodua no).

**Nkyerɛaseɛ na nkyerɛaseɛ a ɛyɛ den:**
- ‘Cold’ (adwene a ɛyɛ den) yɛ ɛho na ɛsɛ sɛ wofa ‘a’: ‘a cold’.
- ‘Flu’ (adwene a ɛyɛ den) yɛ ɛho na ɛsɛ sɛ wofa ‘the’: ‘I have the flu’ anaa ‘I have flu’, nanso ‘the flu’ yɛ ɛho.
- ‘Fever’ (adwene a ɛyɛ den) yɛ ɛho na ɛsɛ sɛ wofa ‘a’: ‘I have a fever’.
- ‘Sore throat’ (adwene a ɛyɛ den) yɛ ɛho na ɛsɛ sɛ wofa ‘a’: ‘I have a sore throat’.
- Ka ho asɛm bi nni ɛho efisɛ ɛnyɛ ɛho: ‘I have a cough’ (anaa ‘to cough’), ‘I have a runny nose’ (anaa ‘I have a runny nose’? wɔ hɔ no, ɛsɛ sɛ wofa ‘a’).

**Kyerɛw:** Wɔ English akyerɛ, yɛnka ‘make’ ma ka ho asɛm sɛnea ɛyɛ wɔ Twi akyerɛ (‘me duele’ = ‘it hurts’ anaa ‘I have pain’).

concept_examples.text: I have a headache.
concept_examples.translation: Me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den.

concept_examples.text: I feel sick.
My stomach hurts.
concept_examples.translation: Me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den.

concept_examples.text: You should see a doctor.

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi akyerɛ, yɛka ‘tengo frío’ anaa ‘tengo un resfriado’ biara, nanso wɔ English akyerɛ, ‘cold’ (adwene a ɛyɛ den) yɛ ɛho na ɛsɛ sɛ wofa ‘a’. ‘Have got’ yɛ ɛho na ɛyɛ nokware. Ma ‘tengo frío’ (adwene a ɛyɛ den), yɛnka ‘I am cold’ anaa ‘I feel cold’, na ɛnyɛ ‘I have cold’.

levels.label: Common symptoms
levels.translation: Ka ho asɛm a ɛyɛ den

examples.translation: Me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den.
examples.note: Fa ‘a’ ma ‘cough’ no. Wɔ Twi akyerɛ, yɛka ‘tengo tos’ biara.

examples.translation: Me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den.
examples.note: ‘Fever’ yɛ ɛho na ɛsɛ sɛ wofa ‘a’, na ɛnyɛ sɛnea ɛyɛ wɔ Twi akyerɛ.

examples.translation: Me wɔ me a me ho yɛ den.
examples.note: ‘Sore throat’ yɛ ɛho a ɛyɛ den. Yɛnka ‘pain in the throat’ biara.

levels.label: Expressing how you feel
levels.translation: Ma adwene ho asɛm

examples.note: Yɛnka ‘feel’ + adwene ma nnomuonyam. Yɛnka ‘I am having dizzy’ biara.
‘Tired’ yɛ adwene, na ɛnyɛ verbo. Wɔ Twi akyerɛ, yɛka ‘estoy cansado’, nanso wɔ English akyerɛ, yɛnka ‘I feel tired’ anaa ‘I am tired’.
Sɛ wɔbisa wo ‘How are you?’ anaa ‘How do you feel?’ a, ɛyɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ den sɛ woka ‘Me nnomuonyam’.

levels.label: Giving and asking about health advice
levels.translation: Ma adwuma na kyerɛw adwuma ho asɛm

examples.note: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wokyerɛw wo ho asɛm a, ɛyɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ den sɛ woka ‘Աnka wo ho asɛm?’. Ɛyɛ ɛho.
Yɛnka ‘should’ + verbo ma adwuma. Yɛnka ‘should to rest’ biara.
Yɛnka ‘take’ ma adwuma, na ɛnyɛ ‘drink’ anaa ‘eat’.
‘Shouldn’t’ yɛ ɛho a ɛyɛ den ma ‘should’. Yɛnka no ma adwuma a ɛnyɛ den.

title: Making requests and offers / Kɔbɔ ahuɔdo ne ma nneɛma
bridge: Wɔ España, yɛnka ‘imperativo’ anaa ‘¿Puedes...?’ ma ahuɔdo, nanso wɔ Twirekang, ‘Can’ ne ‘Could’ ne nneɛma a ɛsɛ paa. Sɛ wopɛ ma nneɛma a, Españafo bɛka ‘¿Quieres que...?’, nanso wɔ Twirekang, yɛnka ‘Can I...?’ anaa ‘Do you want me to...?’. Nya daakye: wɔ Twirekang, ‘Could you...?’ yɛ fɔm a ɛso awaree pii sen ‘Can you...?’, na ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔbɛka imperativo ma ahuɔdo koraa, efisɛ ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ den pii.
rule:
Ma ahuɔdo wɔ Twirekang wɔ A2 level no, yɛnka: 
- 'Can you + verb...?' (ahohia, sɛe) 
- 'Could you + verb...?' (awaree pii ne adwuma pii) 
- 'Would you mind + gerund?' (awaree pii, nanso ɛyɛ den). 
Ma nneɛma: 
- 'Can I + verb...?' (Mepɛ sɛ...) 
- 'Do you want me to + verb...?' (Wopɛ sɛ m...) 
- 'Would you like me to + verb...?' (awaree pii). 
Twe yɛn ara sɛ wɔ Twirekang, verb a ɛwɔ ‘Can’ anaa ‘Could’ nkyɛn no, ɛyɛ ɛho koraa, ɛnyɛ ‘to’. Ma nneɛma a, ka ‘me to’ akyi ‘want’ anaa ‘like’.

concept_examples.text: Can you help me with this?
Could you open the window, please?
concept_examples.translation: Wode ama me a, fa akɔntɔ akyi?

concept_examples.text: Can I give you a hand?
Do you want me to get you a coffee?
concept_examples.translation: Wopɛ sɛ mabɔ kofi bi ma wo?
concept_examples.phonetic: /duː juː wɒnt miː tə ɡet juː ə ˈkɒfi/

common_error.wrong: Do you want that I help you?
common_error.correct: Do you want me to help you?
common_error.explanation: Wɔ España, yɛka ‘¿Quieres que te ayude?’, na mmara bɛtumi atwa ‘that I’. Wɔ Twirekang, ɛho a ɛsɛ no ne ‘want + person + to + verb’, ɛnyɛ ‘that + subject + verb’. Ɛho foforo ne ‘Can I help you?’ a ɛyɛ den pii ne sɛe.

levels.label: Basic requests with Can
levels.translation: Ahuɔdo a ɛho ntease wɔ Can

examples.original: Can you pass me the salt?
examples.translation: Womfa me kwan so bɔ salt a ma me?
examples.note: ɛho a ɛsɛ paa wɔ nneɛma a ɛyɛ da biara. ‘Pass me’ kyerɛ ‘ma me’, nanso sɛ woka ‘can’ a, ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ adwuma pii.

examples.translation: Womfa me kwan so fa door no?
examples.note: Yɛnka ‘can’ ma ahuɔdo a ɛnyɛ awaree pii wɔ nnamfo anaa nuafo nkyɛn.

examples.original: Can you speak more slowly, please?
examples.translation: Womfa me kwan so ka biara pɛpɛɛpɛ, fa me daakye?
examples.note: Bɔ ‘please’ akyi ahuɔdo no akyi sɛ wopɛ sɛ ɛyɛ adwuma pii.

levels.label: Polite requests with Could
levels.translation: Ahuɔdo a ɛyɛ adwuma pii wɔ Could

examples.translation: Wode ama me a, fa me call biosu?
examples.note: Yɛnka ‘could’ sɛ wopɛ sɛ ɛyɛ awaree pii anaa sɛ ɛnyɛ sɛ wahu wo ho pii.

examples.original: Could you bring us the menu, please?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː brɪŋ ʌs ðə ˈmenjuː pliːz/
examples.translation: Wode ama me a, bɔ menu no ma yɛn, fa me daakye?
examples.note: Wɔ restaurant no, ‘could’ yɛ adwuma pii sen ‘can’.

examples.original: Could you help me carry these bags?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː help miː ˈkæri ðiːz bæɡz/
examples.translation: Wode ama me a, ma me kwan so bɔ bags no?
examples.note: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woma wo kwan so bɔ nneɛma a ɛyɛ akɔntɔ a, yɛnka ‘could’ sɛ wopɛ sɛ ɛyɛ awaree pii.

levels.label: Making offers
levels.translation: Ma nneɛma

examples.original: Can I get you something to drink?
examples.phonetic: /kæn aɪ ɡet juː ˈsʌmθɪŋ tə drɪŋk/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mabɔ nneɛma bi ma wo sɛ wo nte asɔ?
examples.note: ɛho a ɛsɛ paa sɛ wopɛ sɛ woma nneɛma, ɛhɔ nhia ‘Wopɛ sɛ wɔmfa nneɛma bi ma wo sɛ wo nte asɔ?’.

examples.original: Do you want me to help you with that?
examples.phonetic: /duː juː wɒnt miː tə help juː wɪð ðæt/
examples.translation: Wopɛ sɛ mama wo kwan so bɔ no?
examples.note: ɛho a ɛsɛ no ne ‘want + me + to’ sɛ wopɛ sɛ woma wo kwan so bɔ nneɛma biara.

examples.original: Would you like me to open the window?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː laɪk miː tə ˈəʊpən ðə ˈwɪndəʊ/
examples.note: ɛyɛ awaree pii sen ‘do you want me to’. Ɛyɛ den wɔ nneɛma a ɛyɛ service anaa wɔ mmara a wohu wo ho pii nkyɛn.

title: Expressing Ability and Possibility / Kasa ntɛm atwa ne nnwim
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka kwan pa biara so a, woyɛ 'sɛe' anaa 'pɛ'. Wɔ English mu, mmom, yɛnkyɛ 'can' (present) ne 'could' (past) ma yɛaka nnwim ne ntɛm atwa. Nanso, 'could' nte sɛ wɔde ma akwan biara a ɛda ada no ho kasa (sɛ 'Could you swim?') na yɛde 'be able to' ma akwan a 'can' nni ho. Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka nnwim a, 'can' ne 'could' kyerɛ nnwim a ɛyɛ paa, na 'may' ne 'might' kyerɛ nnwim a ɛyɛ anigye.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka ntɛm atwa wɔ present tense a, yɛ 'can' + verb (sɛ, 'I can swim'). Wɔ past tense mu, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka ntɛm atwa a, yɛ 'could' + verb (sɛ, 'I could swim when I was young'). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka kwan biara a ɛda ada wɔ past a, yɛ 'was/were able to' (nte sɛ 'could'). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka nnwim a, yɛ 'can' ma nnwim a ɛyɛ paa (sɛ, 'It can rain'), 'could' ma nnwim a ɛda ada anaa conditional (sɛ, 'It could rain later'), 'may' ne 'might' ma nnwim a ɛyɛ anigye (sɛ, 'She may come'). 'can' yɛ 'cannot' anaa 'can't', na 'could' yɛ 'couldn't'. Mmom, nnyɛ 'to' akyi 'can' anaa 'could'.

concept_examples.text: I can speak English and Spanish.
Could you help me, please?
She might be at home now.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔne sɛ ɔwɔ hɔ da biara.

concept_examples.text: We were able to find the hotel after asking.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː wɜːr ˈeɪbəl tə faɪnd ðə hoʊˈtɛl ˈæftər ˈæskɪŋ/

common_error.wrong: I can to play the guitar.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛka 'mɛsɛe' anaa 'mɛpɛ', na wɔbɛka 'to' akyi 'can'. Nanso, wɔ English mu, 'can' ne verb no yɛ kronkron, nni 'to'. Fa so: can + verb, nnte can + to + verb.

levels.label: Ability in the Present
levels.translation: Ntɛm atwa wɔ present

examples.note: Yɛ 'can' ma kyerɛ sɛ wosɛe kwan biara. Fa so sɛ wɔ Twi mu yɛ 'sɛe' anaa 'pɛ', na wɔ English mu yɛ 'can' kronkron.
Wɔmfa ho nhwɛ a, yɛ 'Can' + subject + verb.
Yɛ 'can't' (contraction of 'cannot') ma kyerɛ negative.

levels.label: Ability and Possibility in the Past
levels.translation: Ntɛm atwa ne nnwim wɔ past

examples.original: When I was a child, I could run fast.
examples.phonetic: /wɛn aɪ wəz ə tʃaɪld, aɪ kʊd rʌn fæst/
examples.translation: Sɛ mebɛa ba a, mɛpɛ ntɛm ntɛm.
examples.note: Yɛ 'could' ma kyerɛ ntɛm atwa a ɛda ada wɔ past.

examples.original: I was able to finish the exam yesterday.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wəz ˈeɪbəl tə ˈfɪnɪʃ ði ɪɡˈzæm ˈjɛstərdeɪ/
examples.note: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka kwan biara a ɛda ada wɔ past a, nnyɛ 'could', na yɛ 'was/were able to'.
Wɔ past mu, 'could' ma kyerɛ nnwim.

levels.label: Possibility and Permission
levels.translation: Nnwim ne adwuma

examples.note: Yɛ 'may' ma kyerɛ adwuma anaa sɛ wopɛ sɛ woabɔ wo ho ase.
Yɛ 'might' ma kyerɛ nnwim a ɛyɛ anigye, sɛnea ɛbɛba mu no.
Wɔ English a ɛte sɛe mu, yɛ 'can' ma kyerɛ adwuma.

title: Talking about weather / Kasa mu nsɛm
bridge: Wɔ Spain mu ka de 'hace calor' anaa 'está lloviendo', na ɛkyerɛ wɔn a wɔde 'hacer' anaa 'estar' asɛm. Wɔ England mu, wɔde 'it' kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ subject: 'It is hot', 'It is raining'. Nnka bu a, wɔ England mu, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde subject biara kyerɛw wɔ asɛm mu, nanso wɔ Spain mu, wɔn a wɔde asɛm no wɔn nni hɔ. Nnson a ɛso wɔ England mu, 'weather' nni hɔ sɛ ɛyɛ countable, enti wɔnka 'a weather' anaa 'weathers'.
rule: Saa ɛbɛka nsɛm mu weather wɔ England A2 mu no, hwɛ ɛnɛ ha: 1. 'It is' + adjective: It is sunny, It is cloudy, It is windy, It is cold, It is warm. 2. 'It is' + verb in gerund form for actions: It is raining, It is snowing, It is hailing. 3. 'There is' + noun: There is a storm, There is fog, There is a rainbow. 4. 'There are' + plural nouns: There are clouds, There are showers. Exceptions and uses: 'It is hot' ne 'It is cold' yɛ common, nanso ɛbɛha wo 'It's warm' ne 'It's cool'. Saa ɛbɛkyɛw no, hwɛ 'What's the weather like?' anaa 'How's the weather?' (nni 'How is the weather?'). Yɛn nsa ka sɛ 'weather' nni hɔ sɛ ɛyɛ countable: ɛmmfa 'a weather'.

concept_examples.text: It is sunny today.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛda a ɛyɛ anɔpa no, ɛyɛ sunny.

concept_examples.text: It is raining outside.
It is very cold in winter.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛyɛ cold paa wɔ winter mu.

concept_examples.text: There are some clouds in the sky.
concept_examples.translation: ɛyɛ some clouds wɔ ɔha mu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðər ər sʌm klaʊdz ɪn ðə skaɪ/

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Spain mu ka de 'el tiempo está caliente' anaa 'hace calor', na students no bɛka ɛkɛse. Nanso wɔ England mu, saa ɛbɛka nsɛm mu weather no, yɛde 'it' kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ subject, nni 'the weather'. Sɛ woka sɛ 'the weather is hot' no, ɛmmfa natural; ɛkɛse no yɛ 'It is hot'. Enti, yɛn nsa ka sɛ 'hot' kyerɛ temperature, nni weather pɛ.

levels.label: Basic weather adjectives
levels.translation: Basic weather adjectives

examples.note: Yɛde 'sunny' kyerɛ ɛda a ɛyɛ anɔpa. Wɔ Spain mu, wɔka 'hace sol'.
'Cloudy' kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ clouds paa. Wɔ Spain mu, wɔka 'está nublado'.
'Windy' kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ wind. Mmfa 'wind' (noun).
Kyerɛ temperature a ɛyɛ cold. 'Cold' bɛha object anaa person so.

levels.label: Weather actions
levels.translation: Weather actions

examples.note: Yɛde 'be + -ing' kyerɛ action a ɛyɛ mu. Wɔ Spain mu, wɔka 'está lloviendo'.
Snow bɛyɛ wɔ cold climate mu pɛ. 'Snow' yɛ noun, 'snowing' yɛ verb.
'Hail' yɛ 'hail'. Ɛnyɛ common, nanso ɛyɛ useful.
Expression a ɛkyerɛ sɛ clouds no reba ne sun no betwa.

levels.label: Talking about forecasts
levels.translation: Talking about forecasts

examples.note: Common question for future. De 'like' wɔ mu.

examples.original: It will be rainy on Friday.
examples.note: De 'will' kyerɛ future. 'Rainy' yɛ adjective, 'raining' yɛ action.

examples.original: It is going to snow tonight.
examples.note: 'Going to' yɛ common sɛ ɛyɛ prediction a ɛwɔ hɔ (clouds, etc.).

examples.original: There will be a storm tomorrow.
examples.note: De 'there will be' kyerɛ existence of something wɔ future.
